title: The Empty Frames
inspiredBy: the 1990 theft from the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum in Boston
facts: In the early hours of 18 March 1990, two men dressed as police officers came to a museum's side door and said they were answering a disturbance.
The night guard on duty let them in. The thieves handcuffed the two guards and left them in the basement.
They spent about 81 minutes inside and took 13 works, cutting two paintings from their frames.
The stolen works have never been recovered; the museum still hangs the empty frames where the paintings were.
No one has ever been charged. A large reward is still offered for information.

title: The Missing Smile
inspiredBy: the 1911 theft of the Mona Lisa from the Louvre
facts: In August 1911 a painting was taken from one of the world's most famous museums on a day it was closed to the public.
The thief was a former employee who knew the building; he left with the painting hidden under his work smock.
For more than a day nobody noticed it was gone; staff assumed it had been taken down to be photographed.
Suspicion fell on many people, including well-known artists and writers, before the trail went cold.
Two years later the thief tried to sell it to a dealer in another country and was caught; the painting went back on the wall more famous than before.

title: Ten Layers Down
facts: Over a weekend in February 2003, thieves emptied most of the safe-deposit boxes in a vault two floors below a diamond trading centre.
The vault was said to be protected by many layers of security, including a combination lock, a heat and motion detector, a magnetic field on the door, and guards.
The ring leader had rented office space in the building for about two years and was known there as a trader.
Most of the haul was never found.
The gang was caught partly because of rubbish dumped in a forest by the roadside, which held documents and a half-eaten sandwich.
